dataflow.outcome: derived state can be produced while the repository identity record is invalid
dataflow.sink: batch recovery task mutation and operator-approved outbound enrichment
dataflow.source: adopted repository state with malformed tool-lock and eligible persisted task
dataflow.summary: malformed `.kcs/tool-lock.json` plus recoverable task -> `Repository::open_current()` -> `run_batch()` -> task requeue -> `execute_pending_tasks()` -> markdownize or embedding execution

impact.why: Repository provenance and online-recovery authorization consistency are weakened, and bounded adapter execution or derived-state persistence can occur under malformed tool identity state.

likelihood.why: A supplied-state workflow, eligible recovery task, and operator-run batch command with existing approvals are required.

limitations: The malformed lock does not choose the adapter destination or expose credentials.
Current-byte, secret, media, network, and budget checks remain in force.
The trace does not prove false runtime-profile labeling.

reachability.attacker: lower-trust contributor to copied, shared, migrated, or preseeded KCS scope state
reachability.outcome: batch work proceeds under malformed tool-lock state that sibling commands reject
reachability.summary: The attacker must influence adopted scope state and rely on the operator or automation to run batch recovery with existing network, credential, and budget authorization.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust copied, shared, migrated, or preseeded scope carries a malformed repository tool lock and an otherwise eligible recoverable task. The operator runs `batch resume` or `batch retry`; KCS mutates task state and can issue approved outbound enrichment work even though sibling commands reject the same repository identity state.

codeEvidence.explanation: `Repository::open_current()` only reaches config, scope, manifest, and HEAD checks. It does not parse or validate `.kcs/tool-lock.json`, so each command that depends on the repository tool identity predicate must invoke the CLI helper itself.
codeEvidence.label: Repository open does not validate tool-lock.json

codeEvidence.explanation: `run_batch()` opens the repository and holds the store lock, but neither `resume` nor `retry` calls `validate_repo_tool_lock()` before task mutation or `execute_pending_tasks()`.
codeEvidence.label: Batch recovery mutates task state without the validator

codeEvidence.explanation: Once batch recovery has requeued work, the pending-task executor can drive markdownize and embedding enrichment under the operator's already approved network and budget controls without ever reading the malformed tool lock.
codeEvidence.label: Recovered pending tasks can reach adapter work

codeEvidence.explanation: `index`, `repair`, `reindex`, `status`, `snapshot`, `log`, `diff`, `inspect`, `tag`, and `search` all use the repository tool-lock validation helper before consuming repository state.
codeEvidence.label: Sibling commands invoke the expected control

codeEvidence.explanation: The helper is the fail-closed control that batch recovery omits. It reads the repository lock file and delegates schema validation to `load_tool_lock()`.
codeEvidence.label: The omitted helper parses and validates tool-lock.json

codeEvidence.explanation: A malformed future-version lock already causes sibling command failure when the helper is invoked, so batch recovery is bypassing a concrete existing control rather than an aspirational check.
codeEvidence.label: Existing contract test proves malformed locks are rejected

remediation.summary: Call `validate_repo_tool_lock(&repo)?` under the acquired store lock and before any batch resume/retry task mutation or execution. Keep this schema validation distinct from stronger per-task adapter-profile and destination binding controls.
tests: Create a temporary scope with a future-version `tool-lock.json` and a paused markdownize task, then assert `batch resume` fails before mutating task state.
Repeat with retryable failed and partial markdownize tasks, then assert `batch retry` fails before requeue.
Assert well-formed locks still permit recovery when independent network, secret, byte, and budget gates allow it.
Keep a static guard that `run_batch()` calls `validate_repo_tool_lock()` before `execute_pending_tasks()`.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that commands which mutate or consume adapter-derived repository state must reject malformed `.kcs/tool-lock.json` before work begins. `Repository::open_current()` does not enforce that invariant globally, and `run_batch()` omits the explicit `validate_repo_tool_lock()` call before resume/retry task mutation and pending adapter execution.

summary: KCS batch resume and retry open a repository, take the store lock, mutate recovery task state, and can reach online markdownize or embedding execution without invoking the repository tool-lock validator that sibling commands use.
title: batch recovery bypasses repository tool-lock validation

assertions: `run_batch()` omits `validate_repo_tool_lock()` on both resume and retry branches before task mutation and pending execution.
The existing helper rejects unsupported `tool-lock.json` schema versions when sibling commands invoke it.
limitations: No live adapter request, credential use, or third-party target interaction was performed.
No isolated CLI batch invocation with a malformed lock was captured; the PoC is a non-destructive static regression probe.
The existing validator is schema-oriented and does not prove queued tasks match the current effective adapter profile.
validation.method: saved V10 source trace plus local static regression probe
validation.summary: The saved validation trace and local probe confirm that repository open does not parse the tool lock, batch recovery reaches `execute_pending_tasks()` without `validate_repo_tool_lock()`, and sibling commands reject malformed locks through the existing helper.
